title: DIPS: Optimal Dynamic Index for Poisson πps Sampling

problem.claim: The task is to generate independently sampled subsets from weighted elements, with each element included according to a weight-proportional probability.

gap.claim: Subset-sampling reductions are impractical for dynamic updates because adding or removing an element changes the inclusion probabilities of all elements.

contributions.claim: A dynamic index tailored to Poisson πps sampling.
A recursive weight-based partitioning approach that ultimately uses table lookup.
An approach addressing weight explosion and correlations between elements.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report optimal expected O(1) query time, O(1) index update time, and O(n) space cost.
Empirical evaluations report significant update-time speedups while maintaining consistently competitive query time against subset-sampling-based methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Poisson πps sampling is presented as relevant to domains including influence maximization.
The problem samples weighted elements independently and requires independence across queries.
A subset-sampling reduction becomes impractical under dynamic element updates.
The paper proposes a dynamic index using recursive weight partitioning and table lookup, while addressing weight explosion and element correlations.
Empirical evaluations report faster updates and competitive query time relative to subset-sampling-based methods.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the exact query and update algorithms.
The abstract does not provide evaluation datasets, workloads, baselines, or numerical speedup results.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported complexity or empirical findings.
